transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Daniel, Arjun (Redwood); Lydia, Noah, Priya, Marco (OliveBranch)

Summary: short ops-playground kickoff to validate private deployment connectivity, SSO, and basic perf metrics.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off, quick intros?
[00:12] Lydia Park: hi, Lydia Park, head of platform at OliveBranch, excited to get started.
[00:18] Noah Winters: Noah here, infrastructure and SRE. i'll be your main contact for networking.
[00:22] Priya Rao: Priya, security lead, i'll be owning compliance questions.
[00:26] Marco Diaz: Marco, product, i'll be tracking outcome and metrics.
[00:30] Maya Chen: great, on our side i have Daniel Ruiz, our CSM, and Arjun patel, solutions engineer, arjun will do the technical deep-dive later.
[00:40] Daniel Ruiz: hey all, glad to be here, we'll keep this structured so we have clear next steps.
[00:47] Arjun Patel: morning/afternoon, hi, quick note, we know OliveBranch wants private or VPC mode, so we'll focus on network, SSO, and a pilot config.

[02:05] Marco Diaz: quick question, timeline wise we want something up in two weeks to run sanbox tests — is that feasible?
[02:18] Arjun Patel: two weeks for an ops playground is tight but doable if we have VPC peering and keys; we'll spin up a scaled-down Dedicated/Private node set, run a small load to measure latency and cost.
[02:36] Noah Winters: on peering, we need to confirm IP ranges, route tables and whether we use transit gateway or direct peering. we prefer TGW but open to Redwood suggestions.
[02:52] Arjun Patel: TGW works, we also support direct VPC peering. for pilot we often recommend direct peering because it's simpler and quicker to validate.

[04:10] Priya Rao: security questions — do you have SOC 2 and what about KMS/HSM integration? we need to map to our corporate controls.
[04:24] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood has SOC 2; we'll share the certs and our security whitepaper. for KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in private deployments; i'll attach the integration doc.
[04:38] Priya Rao: cool, and data retention — we need logs for 12 months and audit trails. can you confirm exportability of audit logs?
[04:50] Daniel Ruiz: logs and audit trails are available; retention is configurable in Private and Dedicated. for Hosted we have limited retention tiers. we'll share the observability docs.

[06:15] Lydia Park: for compliance we also need SSO (SAML) and RBAC mapping to our groups; can we do SCIM provisioning?
[06:29] Arjun Patel: yes, SAML SSO plus SCIM for user provisioning is supported. we can map RBAC roles to your AD groups. Priya, we'll send the SAML metadata template.

[08:02] Marco Diaz: performance — what's realistic p95 token latency for the model family we discussed?
[08:12] Arjun Patel: depends on model size and sequence length; for the quantized 7B variants we typically see 60–120 ms p95 for short prompts on a well-configured Dedicated node; on Private it's comparable if you use the same instance types. we will create a small benchmark config for your workload.
[08:36] Noah Winters: what about KV cache and warm-starting? our workflows include multi-turn chat sessions with cached contexts.
[08:48] Arjun Patel: we support KV cache and prefix caching; for chat-heavy workloads we recommend enabling KV caching and tuning batch windows to trade off latency/cost. we'll include cache config suggestions in the runbook.

[10:22] Lydia Park: network egress — any mandatory logging to Redwood hosted endpoints? we're trying to minimize data leaving our VPC.
[10:33] Maya Chen: in Private deployment mode the customer controls egress; telemetry and error traces can be routed to your logging stack. some optional metrics can be sent to Redwood if you opt in.

[12:00] Priya Rao: on encryption in transit, do you support mTLS for intra-service traffic?
[12:08] Arjun Patel: yes, we support TLS and mTLS for internal service meshes if you run the Private package; we'll document cert rotation and trust stores.

[14:05] Marco Diaz: okay, pilot KPIs — what do you usually track for a short ops-playground?
[14:16] Daniel Ruiz: typical pilot KPIs are p95 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, and SSO provisioning time. plus a qualitative evaluation of output quality vs baseline.
[14:32] Marco Diaz: sounds good. we'll add product-level success criteria: < 150ms p95 for short prompts, error rate <0.5% and cost target under $X/1k tokens (we'll fill X after we get numbers).

[16:00] Noah Winters: practical question: who will provide the bastion/jump host? we usually manage bastions for peering tests.
[16:10] Arjun Patel: that's fine, we only need a reachable endpoint and an agreed IP allowlist; we'll run testruns from that host.

[18:05] Priya Rao: can you walk me through the audit log format? we need to ensure PII isn't logged.
[18:18] Daniel Ruiz: audit logs can be filtered; payload logging is disabled by default in Private. we'll share schema and sample logs.

[20:00] Lydia Park: who are the escalation contacts during the pilot?
[20:06] Maya Chen: primary contact is Daniel for ops and CSM; Arjun is escalation for technical, and i am the AE for contract / procurement questions.

[22:00] Marco Diaz: procurement — any paperwork we should expect? NDA is done. Is there a PO or MSA?
[22:12] Maya Chen: we have a standard MSA for Private deployments; we'll send a draft for legal review. Procurement usually requests scope + estimated monthly committed spend for Dedicated.

[24:00] Noah Winters: ok final networking note: we'll send VPC cidr and a short window for peering on Monday.
[24:08] Maya Chen: perfect, that will let Arjun spin up the sample cluster.

[26:00] Arjun Patel: next technical touchpoint — propose a 60-minute deep-dive on private deployment networking and perf tooling; goal: deliver a pilot topology and perf config. availability week of Nov 30?
[26:14] Lydia Park: works for us that week, prefer Nov 30 or Dec 1.

[28:00] Daniel Ruiz: i'll draft the pilot success metrics doc and invite the stakeholder group; we'll include a 2-week runbook with checkpoints at day 3, day 7, day 14.

[30:00] Priya Rao: small thing — we need to confirm where keys are stored during the pilot; KMS only.
[30:08] Arjun Patel: correct, for Private we use customer KMS for model keys where required; we will not store unencrypted keys in Redwood control plane.

[32:00] Marco Diaz: any recommended tooling to capture token costs per route?
[32:10] Daniel Ruiz: Redwood Console provides per-route token cost breakdowns and will export CSV. we'll give you access to a staging console.

[34:00] Lydia Park: ok let's recap and confirm owners.
[34:08] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Maya to send onboarding runbook, SAML/SCIM templates, SOC2 certs. 2) Noah to send VPC details and allowlist. 3) Arjun to prepare pilot perf config. 4) Daniel to prepare pilot KPIs and schedule checks. 5) Priya to send KMS/retention constraints. agreed?
[34:36] Priya Rao: agreed.
[34:40] Noah Winters: agreed.
[34:44] Lydia Park: agreed.

[36:00] Maya Chen: great — we'll follow up with the runbook and schedule a deep-dive. any last questions?
[36:12] Marco Diaz: none from me.
[36:16] Priya Rao: one last quick — can we get a short note on how fallbacks work if a model variant is unavailable?
[36:23] Arjun Patel: yes, fallback policies are part of routing config; we can set prioritized model variants and automatic fallbacks to cheaper families. i'll include examples in the runbook.

[38:00] Daniel Ruiz: ok i'll send calendar invites for the two items: runbook delivery and networking deep-dive.
[38:08] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll close out and send notes.
[38:12] Lydia Park: thanks, bye.
[38:15] Noah Winters: thanks, bye.
[38:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: some model/term names may be mistranscribed (e.g., TGW as T-G-W or transit gateway), occasional speaker label swap; audio quality good.
